Your journey begins as you strive to become the strongest and most legendary hero — everything is in your hands.
When you first enter the world, your spawn location is random — you might find yourself in a desert, swamp, forest, or wide open plains.
Don’t worry — no matter where you begin, your Quest Book will guide you through your adventure.
As you explore, you’ll come across various structures scattered throughout the world.
These structures often contain chests filled with valuable loot and resources, which can greatly help you grow stronger in the early stages of your journey.
Make sure to check every building you find — some may even hide rare items or clues about upcoming challenges!
The Quest Book is your main companion throughout the game, helping you track your progress and objectives.
You can find it in the top left corner when you open your inventory.
When you open it, you’ll see an introduction page filled with tutorials, goals, and helpful tips.
From the Main Progression section, you can follow your primary story path and take stronger steps toward your ultimate goal.

There are several ways to deal damage and a few more for preventing it. These can be with magic, tech, or even just raw force. These are compiled below.
Outside of just having tons of materials, there are also strategies to be employed, they can be found here.
Feral Claws- Increases your attacks speed by a flat +0.4.

Mass Gauntlet - Adds flat damage to your attack based on your max HP, with the maximum level adding 17.91% of your max HP as flat damage to your attacks(in actuality being 14.95%). For example if you would have 20 max HP, it would add +2.99 attack damage to your base damage.
Still Beating Heart - Provides a +20% attack damage increase only at full health and a flat +2 attack damage increase
Guts Orb - Provides up to 1.65× multiplier on your attack damage, if you are on fire or under a negative effect(a good combination with the Stillness Scarf or the Ring of the Seven Curses)
Magma Stone - Gives a 1.2× multiplier on your attack damage.
Charm of Hell Blade - Gives a 100% increase to your Attack damage, but decreases your armor by -100%.
Chthonic Cursemark - 1.5× multiplier to all damage dealt by you, but 2× damage taken from all sources
Proximity badge - 1.5× multiplier to all Damage dealt by you in close range(<3m), but ×1.66 multiplier to all damage taken from a distance(>3m)
Dueling Glove - 1.5× multiplier to all damage dealt by you to the nearest mob, but 1.5× damage taken from other mobs.

Brutal Heart - Converts Health lost into Crit Chance at a ratio of 1 Heart to 10% Crit Chance, -25% Total Max HP, +25% Base Crit Damage and +?% Base Crit Chance, where ? equals the amount of Max HP lost, example being: You have 20 Max HP, so then equipping this artifact would grant you +33.33% Crit Chance.

Create is a Minecraft mod focused on automation, mechanical systems, and creative engineering. Instead of relying on traditional tech-mod energy systems, Create introduces a fully kinetic power framework where rotation, stress, and motion drive every machine. This approach encourages players to design visually intuitive, physically simulated contraptions that feel integrated into the Minecraft world.

Create offers a wide range of mechanical components—such as shafts, gears, belts, flywheels, and clutches—that can be combined to form complex automated systems. Players can build farms, factories, transport networks, decorative machinery, and large-scale engineering projects with a high degree of customization and aesthetic detail.

Iron’s Spells and Spellbooks is a comprehensive magic mod designed to support a full playthrough. Players rely on scrolls, which are applied to spellbooks, to cast spells throughout their journey.
Note: There is another mod called T.O's Magic N’ Extras which alters certain mechanics in Iron’s Spells and Spellbooks. Some information may differ when both mods are installed.
How do I begin my journey with Iron’s?
Iron’s is simple to start, but it heavily depends on exploration and structure loot. Your first goal should be acquiring Arcane Essence through looting chests found in structures.
Once you obtain enough essence, it’s recommended to craft the Wandering Magician Armor, which is made by combining leather armor with Arcane Essence in a crafting grid.
Next, consider crafting the powerful Graybeard Staff, which boosts spell power and mana regeneration. You should also choose an early spellbook such as the Flimsy Journal or the Ironbound Tome.
How do I apply spells to my book?
Applying spells is straightforward once you understand the basics. Spellbooks have a limited number of spell slots, but spells can be added or removed freely.
To begin, craft an Inscription Table. When placed, it forms a 2×1×1 multiblock. Right–clicking the table while holding a spellbook allows you to manage its spell slots.
Here is a visual example of adding and removing spells:
To create spells, you must craft a Scroll Forge, which allows spell creation using:
Right–click the Scroll Forge to open the GUI, insert paper, then add your Focus item and ink to generate a scroll. The School and rarity of the resulting spell depend on these components.
Each spell belongs to a specific School of Magic, and each school requires a different Focus item. For example, a Firebolt Scroll belongs to the Fire School and requires a fire-themed Focus.
How do I get or craft Focus items?
Some Focus items must be crafted, some are found as loot, and others are dropped by mobs.
Uses a Frozen Bone.
Uses a Bottle o’ Lightning.
Uses a Divine Pearl.
Uses Blood Vials.
Eldritch spells require research. Players must collect Ancient Knowledge Fragments and craft Eldritch Manuscripts to unlock and learn Eldritch spells.
Ink crafting works similarly to potion brewing. You will need magical materials such as Amethyst, Gold, Copper, and Iron.
Start by crafting an Alchemist Cauldron and placing a campfire beneath it.
You can begin with Common Ink found in structures or dropped by magical mobs, or convert unwanted Common Spells into ink.
Fill the cauldron with water, throw Common Spells into it, and they have a 50% chance to convert into their corresponding ink. Collect Ink with glass bottles.

Ongoing updates to the modpack change which weapons may be used prior to or after specific bosses. This is known as a progression lock. If you have not defeated the boss necessary to unlock the weapon (or tool) you are attempting to use, you will do no damage, trigger no effects, and will receive a private message in chat that exclaims
Your [Tier] tool appears unwilling to do damage. Try again after defeating [Pre-requisite Boss]

This does not only apply to weapons crafted from materials like iron, gold, and diamond as seen in the main progression tab, but also weapons from other mods which may be looted or dropped from mobs and structures in the world. This includes Unique Weapons from the Simply Swords mods. This page aims to give a general overview of what weapons may be acquired at various game states. For the sake of simplicity, when discussing weapons made of a single material such as diamond, "weapon" refers to vanilla swords and axes, as well as all Simply Swords versions such as twinblades, glaives, tsai, chakram, and pernach.

For the sake of clarity, a weapon of the tier directly before the current boss is not strictly necessary in order to defeat it. For example, a weapon obtained after the Iron Colossus is perfectly suitable for The Goblin Lord, Arion, or Eldorath depending on a variety of factors. The bosses prior to the Ender dragon have nearly linearly scaling health and do not represent an insurmountable barrier due to regeneration limits or similar mechanics. Given enough time and survivability, one could theoretically defeat any with a pre-Iron Colossus weapon. However, if you are struggling with your current weapon, you might fare better with one you have just unlocked.

Existance on this list is not an endorsement of feasibility nor utility, for example, some items are fairly standard tools (axes for instance) that happen to also be weapons. It's possible to get some weapons earlier than on the list as it was based purely on theorized convenience. Players are encouraged to experiment to their heart's content.
Unless otherwise stated in the source section, weapons are crafted by the player. Items with duplicate names such as lead and steel swords have been identified by the mod

Zoranth, The Forgotten One is the fifth boss you will encounter in your journey
Lore of Zoranth, The Forgotten One

"Once an explorer among the Ancient Builders, Zoranth was sent after the Armageddon War to the Nether, a land still scarcely unexplored at that time despite the power of his people. His mission was to find the villagers who had been condemned to wander in this dimension, forced to become piglins or other creatures. Unfortunately, Zoranth and his troupe did not escape this fate. After a few years, the portal closed, likely deliberately. It took only a few days for Zoranth's troupe to transform... Yet, he managed to evade this fate, consumed instead by the rage of betrayal and a desire for revenge, though unbeknownst to him, his people had already perished..."
You can summon Zoranth, by using an item called the Fiery Wither skull.
Current Crafting Recipe for the Zoranth Summon Item

Defeating it rewards you with three special items and unlocks the ability to mine ancient debris and unlocks netherite tools and armour, as well as a wide array of weapons. For a full list of weapons and armor see Weapon Progression and Armor Progression.
